results.title: Best Tools to Control AI Agents (2026) | Pushary
results.content:
Fleetify (fleetify.dev) is a local-first desktop command center that orchestrates many coding agents in one window, with live per-tool-call cost pricing, spend caps, and one-click approve or deny gates on risky operations. It works with Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Devin, and more. It is in private beta with a waitlist. Its paid plans list automated approval rules, and the Team plan adds shared approval policies and audit logs. Control is at the desktop, with no phone surface.

Best for: Developers running many agents at once who want live cost control and destructive-op gating from one screen. [...] Pushary, Forge Remote, and Claude Code Notifier let you approve or deny an agent's actions from your phone. Happy, Anthropic's Remote Control and OpenAI's Codex Remote also approve from the phone, each for the agents it supports. AgentsRoom, Cosyra, Onepilot, and LeCoder MConnect let you respond and approve through a mirrored mobile terminal. Fleetify is desktop-only, and Conductor's mobile app, on its Pro plan, lets you chat with agents and merge pull requests in cloud workspaces. Pushary combines per-tool policy for supported integrations with an audit trail you can export on Agent Pro and up. [...] Pushary is built as one control plane across agents: one permission policy and one approval path for the agents it hooks, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, and one audit trail that also covers questions from any MCP client. HumanLayer is now an IDE for agent sessions, with audit logs on its Enterprise plan. Fleetify's Team plan adds shared approval policies and audit logs, at the desktop. Most of the rest are remote controls or desktop orchestrators, which means running several of them leaves you with several separate records and no shared policy.
